segments.title: What is Binary Search?
segments.narration: Binary search is a fast way to locate a target value in a sorted list by repeatedly halving the search range.

segments.title: Why Sorting Matters
segments.narration: The algorithm only works when the data is sorted, because it relies on ordering to decide which half to discard.

segments.title: Core Idea
segments.narration: We compare the target with the middle element: if equal we’re done, if smaller we search left, if larger we search right.
segments.on_screen: Compare target ↔ middle → left / right half

segments.title: Iterative Steps
segments.narration: Set low to 0 and high to n‑1. While low ≤ high, compute mid, check array[mid], and adjust low or high accordingly.

segments.title: Complexity Analysis
segments.narration: Binary search runs in O(log n) time, O(1) space iteratively, and O(log n) space recursively because of the call stack.
segments.on_screen: Time: O(log n) • Space: Iterative O(1) • Recursive O(log n)

segments.title: Example Walkthrough
segments.narration: In [2,4,6,8,10,12], searching for 8: first mid=6 (index2) → target larger, search right half; next mid=8 (index3) → found.

segments.title: Where It’s Used
segments.narration: Binary search powers dictionary lookups, database indexing, and helps find insertion points in many algorithms.
